probe.text_sample: Your Page Title Outkast ® Work Services About Careers Journal Contact Overview Buy Outkast Menu Outkast ® Close Work Services About Careers Journal Contact Overview Buy Outkast How to write a pitch an editor finishes Most pitches are deleted after the subject line. Here is how we write the ones that get read to the end. Published 22 September 2026 Reading time 2 min read An editor on a national desk gets somewhere between two and four hundred pitches a week. They read the subject line of all of them, the first sentence of maybe a third, and the whole thing of a handful. Everything we teach new press officers is about getting into that handful. Write to one person A pitch that could go to anyone goes to no one. Before we write a word, we read the last six weeks of the person we are writing to and find the piece our story would sit next to. The first line names it. Not to flatter, but to show we know what they actually run. Lead with the story, not the brand Editors do not cover brands, they cover stories that happen to involve one. “Porto roaster launches first retail blend” is a press release. “The roaster who has tasted every bag he has sold for six years” is a story.
